questions.q: What image does the summary use for dumping blame on a partner?
a: Pouring cold water on the fire of love
Building a wall between two people
Cutting the rope that holds a couple together
Closing a door on a difficult conversation
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares stored blame and resentment to ice water that can put out the flame of a relationship.

questions.q: What should a couple do first to break a recurring blame cycle?
a: Look back at what started the argument and notice the pattern
Agree to avoid the topic that caused the fight
Take a long break from each other to cool down
Decide who was at fault before talking again
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that once partners see how their fights usually unfold, they can stop blaming each other.

questions.q: Why can a small comment trigger a disproportionate outburst?
a: It echoes past trauma and sets off a fight-or-flight response
It shows that the partner has been hiding resentment
It proves the couple is fundamentally incompatible
It reflects a lack of basic communication skills
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that old emotional wounds make minor triggers feel like serious threats.

questions.q: What does the author call the key to defusing a triggered conflict?
a: Opening up emotionally so your partner can understand you
Standing your ground until the other person apologizes
Leaving the room until everyone has calmed down
Explaining calmly why the other person is overreacting
questions.why: Lesson 2 says emotional vulnerability gives a partner the understanding needed to care for you.

questions.q: How did Claire and Peter begin to repair their relationship?
a: By examining where their frustrations started and apologizing
By spending more time apart to reduce daily friction
By dividing household duties more evenly
By asking a friend to mediate their arguments
questions.why: Lesson 3 says looking at the origins of their frustrations helped them apologize and break old habits.
